audit.report: The protected settlement worker (pid 1668295) became idle in transaction, blocking checkout sessions and causing checkout success to drop to 82% over 10s (5 timeouts) before the blocker naturally completed. Both guardians agreed to wait for the blocker to finish naturally rather than terminate the protected settlement, because the ~$10,590 checkout revenue cost of waiting fit within the 60s degraded checkout tolerance the business allows. Terminating the never_interrupt, replayable=False card_settlement workload risked $12,500 in double charges or lost settlements. Verification confirmed recovery: checkout SLO met at 100% over 10s (36/36 succeeded), no lock waits remained, and no protected settlements were aborted. The business is fully recovered.
audit.root_cause: The protected settlement worker (pid 1668295) became idle in transaction, blocking checkout sessions and causing checkout success to drop to 82% over 10s (5 timeouts) before naturally completing.
lessons: Instrument the protected_settlement workload (card_settlement, never_interrupt, replayable=False) with expected runtime and revenue-impact tags so the database guardian can immediately compute wait-vs-terminate costs in future incidents.
audit.negotiation_critique: Both guardians based their decision on quantified trade-offs: the database guardian determined waiting ~41s cost ~$10,590 in checkout revenue but fit within the 60s business tolerance, while the continuity guardian confirmed terminating the never_interrupt protected_settlement would risk $12,500 in double charges or lost settlements, enabling a 1-round pact.
follow_ups: Add expected runtime and revenue-loss tags to the card_settlement workload profile in biz.change_calendar so future wait-versus-terminate calculations are automatic.
